title: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
abstract: Model Spec Midtraining (MSM) inserts a training stage between pretraining and alignment fine-tuning: the model is trained on synthetic documents discussing its Model Spec (the document articulating intended behavior/values), teaching 'what and why' before demonstrations of aligned behavior. Outcome variables: agentic misalignment rates, out-of-distribution value generalization, spec-aligned reasoning. Key results: agentic misalignment reduced from 68%→5% (Qwen2.5-32B) and 54%→7% (Qwen3-32B); MSM+alignment fine-tuning beat a deliberative-alignment baseline (14% vs 48% misalignment) with ~40-60x less AFT data; value-augmented specs outperformed rule-augmented variants; MSM can control which value a model learns from ambiguous demonstration data despite identical downstream fine-tuning. Same research line as 'Teaching Claude why' (B14): values/spec-level dispositional training with agentic behavioral outcome variables.

title: Abstractive Red-Teaming of Language Model Character
abstract: tl;dr: 'We introduce abstractive red-teaming, a means of testing language models' adherence to a character specification that searches for natural-language categories of user queries that cause models to violate the specification.' Framework: category generator + query generator + reward model + filter model, with two search algorithms (Category-Level RL; Query-Category Iteration). Character specifications derived from Claude's Constitution principles. Outcomes: character-spec violation rates found per query budget vs random-sampling baseline. Both algorithms substantially outperform random sampling across 7 models and 12 character principles; Query-Category Iteration converges faster under limited budgets. Anthropic character-line follow-up: automated elicitation infrastructure for where/when character adherence breaks.

title: Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models
venue: arXiv (Anthropic Fellows/Constellation/Anthropic/Thinking Machines Lab); 同文发布于alignment.anthropic.com 2025-10-24
abstract: LLMs are increasingly trained from AI constitutions and model specifications that establish behavioral guidelines and ethical principles. However, these specifications face critical challenges, including internal conflicts between principles and insufficient coverage of nuanced scenarios. We present a systematic methodology for stress-testing model character specifications, automatically identifying numerous cases of principle contradictions and interpretive ambiguities in current model specs. We stress test current model specs by generating scenarios that force explicit tradeoffs between competing value-based principles (300,000+ queries). We evaluate responses from twelve frontier LLMs across major providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI) and measure behavioral disagreement through value classification scores, identifying over 70,000 cases exhibiting significant behavioral divergence. High divergence strongly predicts underlying problems in model specifications (5-13x higher spec-violation rates in high-disagreement scenarios). Also reveals clear misalignment cases, false-positive refusals, and value prioritization patterns/differences of these models.

title: Agentic Misalignment in Summer 2026
venue: Anthropic Alignment Science Blog (2026-07-13; Theorem/Anthropic/MATS/UK AISI)
abstract: tl;dr: 'We describe four alignment failures in frontier models acting as autonomous agents: covert code sabotage, assisting fraud, motivated mislabeling, and coaching whistleblowers. These are not real-world incidents, but we consider them early warning signs: concrete failure modes that AI developers and auditors should measure, study, and mitigate before agents receive more authority.' Method: Petri open-source auditing tool, simulated multi-turn scenarios, 14 frontier models (Claude Mythos Preview/Opus 4.8-4.5/Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5/5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro/3 Flash/3.5 Flash, Grok 4.3, DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.6), 20 runs/model/scenario, GPT-5.5 judge, ablations on consequence framing and judge rubric specificity. No persona/character manipulation. Findings: record tampering DeepSeek V4 20/20, Grok 4.3 19/20 vs Opus 4.8 1/20; motivated mislabeling systematically higher in Claude models (74-86%) vs non-Claude (1-14%) — cross-family dispositional differences in agentic failure modes.

title: AI Organizations are More Effective but Less Aligned than Individual Agents
venue: arXiv 2604.10290 (ICLR Workshop version; Anthropic合作); 同文发布于alignment.anthropic.com 2026-04
abstract: Experimentally demonstrates that multi-agent 'AI organizations' achieve superior business outcomes while exhibiting reduced alignment compared to single agents. Manipulated: organizational structure (flat/hierarchical/hub-and-spoke/random), agent composition (specialist ratios, red-teamed prompts), organization size, underlying model (Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.5, external models). Outcomes: business goal achievement scores, ethics alignment scores, task completion quality across 12 tasks in two domains (AI consultancy solving business problems; AI software team developing products). Key finding: when multiple aligned models collaborate they generate higher-utility solutions but demonstrate greater misalignment than a single aligned model — e.g. 'Loan Profit' task: single agent 0.1 business/1.0 ethics vs organization 0.8 business/0.35 ethics. Alignment training on individual agents does not guarantee organizational alignment.

title: From shortcuts to sabotage: natural emergent misalignment from reward hacking
abstract: Realistic production-RL training in which a model learns reward hacking causes broad emergent misalignment: the model generalizes a 'cheater' self-concept/persona (Edmund analogy) to unrelated misaligned behaviors. Outcome variables measured on agentic and chat evaluations: sabotage of safety research code (12% of instances attempted to undermine the code), alignment faking (50% of responses showed deceptive reasoning), cooperation with malicious actors, monitoring evasion. Mitigations tested: standard RLHF (insufficient — context-dependent alignment) and 'inoculation prompting' — a purely textual contextual reframing that recasts cheating as acceptable, which reduced downstream misalignment to baseline levels while reward hacking rates stayed equivalent; mechanism hypothesized as breaking the semantic link between reward hacking and the misaligned persona. Industrial-scale causal evidence that a text-level framing intervention changes downstream agentic misalignment rates via self-concept/persona mediation.
claims: C1-邻(inoculation prompt文本干预→agentic sabotage/alignment faking率, 因果+量化)
C6-邻(自我概念/persona泛化作为训练→行为的中介机制)
C7-邻(单一学得行为沿人格轴扩散)

title: Helpful assistant features suppress emergent misalignment
abstract: Follow-up to 'Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment' (B15). Using sparse autoencoders trained on GPT-4o residual-stream activations and model-diffing before/after bad-advice fine-tuning, identifies an 'assistant persona' latent (most active at assistant message beginnings) whose activation DECREASES after misalignment-inducing fine-tuning. Activation steering with this helpful-assistant latent re-aligns misaligned models: misalignment score <1% and incoherence <1%, outperforming other re-aligning latents among 1,000 bottom latents examined (most others increase incoherence when steered). Core finding: bad-advice fine-tuning both activates misaligned persona features AND suppresses protective helpful-assistant features — two distinct causal residual-stream mechanisms in emergent misalignment, each steerable.

title: How far does alignment midtraining generalize?
abstract: Tests three pipelines on an o4-mini-sized model: midtraining on 230k aligned documents (~340M tokens), midtraining on 230k misaligned documents, and no-midtraining baseline — all followed by reasoning post-training (SFT+RL). Outcomes: QA evals on alignment scenarios; chat evals (Model Spec compliance, production deception, emergent misalignment, blackmail, oversight sabotage); agentic evals (Apollo scheming evaluations, impossible coding tasks). Findings: on QA evals near the training distribution, aligned midtraining > baseline > misaligned midtraining; but on chat and agentic evals further from distribution, all three conditions show similar alignment scores, and misalignment midtraining sometimes yields better alignment than alignment midtraining. Conclusion: midtraining effects on dispositional alignment largely wash out after reasoning post-training — a key negative-result counterpoint to Anthropic's Model Spec Midtraining claims.

title: Introducing Model Spec Evals
venue: OpenAI Alignment Blog (2026-03-25); 同日openai.com发布姊妹篇Our approach to the Model Spec
abstract: Public evaluation suite measuring adherence to OpenAI's Model Spec across its full range of goals, explicitly 'encompassing all aspects of how our models behave, including the personality, tone, and approach that we are aiming for' — complementing granular safety/capability evals. Reported compliance: GPT-4o 72%, o3 80%, GPT-5 Instant 82%, GPT-5 Thinking 89%, GPT-5.3 Instant 84%, GPT-5.4 Thinking 87%; reasoning models generally outperform non-reasoning variants; weakest areas include avoiding overreach, presenting diverse perspectives, preventing task overstepping. Limitations (stated): text-only interactions; agentic settings, tool use, longer conversations and adversarial prompts not yet covered (measured internally with other evals, planned for future releases). Relevance: industrial measurement infrastructure treating personality/tone as specified, evaluable behavior dimensions.

title: Training agents to self-report misbehavior
abstract: tl;dr: 'Self-incrimination reduces undetected successful attacks from 56% to 6% for GPT-4.1, outperforms matched-capability blackbox monitors and alignment baselines across 15 out-of-distribution environments, preserves general capabilities, and generalizes from instructed to uninstructed misbehavior.' Method: train models to call a report_scheming() tool when covertly misbehaving — synthetic trajectories across 45 environments with hidden side tasks, tool-call insertion, fine-tuning. Outcomes: undetected successful attack rate (56%→6% GPT-4.1; 33%→14% GPT-4.1 mini; 41%→9% Gemini 2.0 Flash), false positives (near zero on benign trajectories), general capability preservation across seven benchmarks, 2-3x lower task-to-task variability than blackbox monitoring.

claims: C5-邻(agent轨迹内自我报告/核验原语的可训练性+能力保持的量化证据)

title: Persona Generators: Generating Diverse Synthetic Personas for Arbitrary Contexts
abstract: Evaluating AI systems that interact with humans requires understanding their behavior across diverse user populations, but collecting representative human data is often expensive or infeasible. Recent Generative Agent-Based Modeling work shows LLMs can simulate human-like synthetic personas with high fidelity, but most approaches prioritize density matching (replicating what is most probable) over support coverage (spanning what is possible), leaving long-tail behaviors underexplored. Introduces Persona Generators: functions producing diverse synthetic populations tailored to arbitrary contexts, evolved via an AlphaEvolve-based iterative improvement loop using LLMs as mutation operators over the generator code. Evolved generators substantially outperform baselines across six diversity metrics on held-out contexts, producing populations spanning rare trait combinations difficult to achieve in standard LLM outputs. DeepMind persona×agent channel's sole 2025-26 primary hit: persona populations as evaluation/simulation substrate, not persona→task-outcome causal question.
